newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X rises on encouraging reports.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X rises on encouraging reports.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd zoomed back into action on Wednesday after investors were encouraged by reports that held out hope for an open auction for Bre-X and its huge Busang gold deposit, analyts said.
Shares in Bre-X were up C$0.55 to C$22.25 in trading of 356,000 shares by mid-morning. Placer Dome Inc, which wants to bid on Bre-X, rose C$0.15 to C$28.05 in heavy trading of 868,000 shares.
But Barrick Gold Corp, which has been told by the Indonesian government to form a joint venture with Bre-X, was down C$0.15 to C$36.65.
Bre-X's shares rose after a newspaper reported that Bre-X believes it has found a way to control Busang without Barrick.

The Toronto Globe and Mail also said Bre-X appears ready to tell the Indonesian government within days that a deal with Barrick is unworkable and the Indonesian government should hold an auction for the rights to develop Busang.

But in an interview Wednesday morning, Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said Bre-X was in the midst of negotiations with its Indonesian partners, and the outcome of its proposed deal with Barrick would depend on the outcome of the talks with its Indonesian partners.
"Until we can conclude things with our partners, we cannot make any comments as to which direction we're going to proceed in," McAnulty said from Calgary.
"What we're saying is we'll wait and see what the outcome of meetings with Mr. Hasan are, and that will give us indications on how to proceed from here," McAnulty said.
Powerful Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan controls PT Askatindo and PT Amsya Lyna, two of Bre-X's partners on Busang.
McAnulty denied that the company was ready to tell the Indonesian government that a deal with Barrick was unworkable.
Meanwhile, industry sources said Barrick was also in discussions with Hasan in Indonesia.
Bre-X chief executive David Walsh, Placer Dome chief executive John Willson and top ranking Barrick officials were all in Jakarta to sort out details of the deal.
The talks with Hasan were proceeding well, McAnulty said.
"We do expect an agreement in short order."
He said the company had held out hope for weeks the process would be opened up to an auction.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said it was premature to suggest Barrick had been frozen out of a deal for Busang.
"Barrick believes it is premature to reach a conclusion about any arrangements being satisfactory or not with Askatindo until discussions are completed," Borg said in a phone interview.
"The government has asked us to make satisfactory arrangements, and if we can, then everything is full steam ahead with Barrick and Bre-X and Askatindo."
In Vancouver, a spokesman for Placer Dome said there were no developments in the company's bid to proceed with its US$5 billion offer to merge with Bre-X.
((Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104))
